scope_guardrail: These are house-authored mathematical explanations, not sourced artifacts or measured plots. Use engineering j, exp(+j omega n) for synthesis/rotation, exp(-j omega n) for analysis projections, phase in (-pi,pi] with -pi displayed as +pi, and the explicit engineering-phasor versus two-sided-coefficient scale. Do not introduce a DFT-bin axis, analog reconstruction claim, z-plane/ROC treatment, interpolated sample curve, or causal-start eigenfunction claim.

resolved_conventions: The engineering phasor is P=A exp(j phi); each two-sided conjugate coefficient has magnitude A/2.
The course analysis sign gives I=(2/N) sum x cos and Q=-(2/N) sum x sin, so I+jQ=A exp(j phi) on the declared orthogonal interval.
Displayed phase uses (-pi,pi], making the n=2 quarter-turn phase +pi rather than -pi.
The three-tap eigenfunction factorization is exact at every index only for an eternal complex exponential; a causal start has two partial-overlap outputs.

format_decisions.reason: The course key_image requires figures/phasor-projections.svg, and the visual is a small unit-circle/stem construction with only short labels and exact four-sample values.
The coordinate geometry must bind to several typeset formulas and a responsive numeric ledger; shared KaTeX and HTML layout are safer than hand-positioned SVG formula text.

The lesson asks the learner to reveal one counter-rotating component, then its conjugate, then their real sum. The geometry is simple, labels are short, and file frames make a pixel-identical one-delta sequence straightforward.

The forward handoff contains a long complex multiplier, gain and phase annotations, and an eternal-input qualification. HTML plus KaTeX preserves the formula and allows numbered cards to stack on mobile.

figures.pedagogical_necessity: This binds the geometric components to the exact rectangular/polar conversion and atan2 argument order. It prevents the common quadrant and sign mistakes without duplicating the later detector.
figures.source_status: House component inspired by Schaedler Lessons 16-17 and Osgood Appendix A.2; recreate the idea, not source layout.
figures.embed: <Figure name="PhasorCoordinateLedger" alt="The complex number one plus j is decomposed into an amber horizontal coordinate I equals one, a blue vertical coordinate Q equals one, magnitude square root of two, and phase pi over four, beside matching rectangular and polar formulas." caption="Rectangular coordinates are convenient for addition; magnitude and angle are convenient for repeated rotation." />
figures.teaching_claim: For z=1+j, rectangular coordinates (I,Q)=(1,1) and polar coordinates (A,theta)=(sqrt(2),pi/4) describe the same point, with theta obtained from atan2(Q,I).
figures.composition: A responsive two-part component. One side is a square complex-plane SVG for z=1+j with amber horizontal I=1, blue vertical Q=1, a currentColor radial magnitude arrow, and a phase arc. The other side is an HTML/KaTeX ledger binding z=I+jQ=Ae^(j theta), A=sqrt(I^2+Q^2)=sqrt(2), and theta=atan2(Q,I)=pi/4. Put formulas outside SVG via the shared M component.

figures.embed: <Figure name="ComplexModeEigenfunction" alt="An eternal complex exponential enters a three-tap LTI filter and exits at the same discrete frequency multiplied by H of e to the j omega, whose magnitude supplies gain and whose angle supplies phase shift." caption="An eternal complex mode survives an LTI system unchanged in frequency; one complex multiplier records gain and phase shift." />
figures.teaching_claim: For an eternal input exp(j omega n), a three-tap LTI system preserves omega and multiplies the mode by H(exp(j omega))=h0+h1exp(-j omega)+h2exp(-j2 omega).
figures.composition: Use three numbered responsive cards rather than one wide unbreakable equation: (1) eternal input x[n]=exp(j omega n), n in Z; (2) three-tap LTI sum with h0,h1,h2; (3) output H(exp(j omega))exp(j omega n). A short bottom ledger binds amber exp(j omega n) to 'same omega' and blue H to '|H| gain' and 'angle H phase'. Wide layout reads left-to-right with rightward connectors; narrow layout stacks by number and suppresses connectors rather than drawing downward arrows.
